run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-17T23:26:45Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: Observed: the RequestErrorRate alert on otel-demo/frontend-proxy coincides with a window in which the ad service served no requests and the frontend's calls to ad were refused at the connection level (gRPC status 14, 'connect ECONNREFUSED 100.70.197.56:8080'), producing frontend HTTP 500s that frontend-proxy recorded as its own error spans (ingress and router frontend egress STATUS_CODE_ERROR). frontend-proxy's per-5m error-span increase moved from a 0–4.4 baseline to 121.1 at 23:29:45Z, peaked at 614.4 at 23:33:45Z and returned to 4.4 at 23:41:45Z; the per-minute series places the onset between 23:29:00Z and 23:30:00Z and the end by 23:38:00Z. The single-replica ad Deployment was restarted at 23:28:05Z (pod-template annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt, same image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-ad, new ReplicaSet ad-785b4464f5); its new pod ad-785b4464f5-9bshh ran and was Ready with 0 restarts from 23:28:07Z but wrote no log lines and served no GetAds spans until ~23:36:20Z, while its container was throttled in 96–100% of CFS periods. Service ad has no NetworkPolicy or ResourceQuota obstruction, and its selector/endpoints match the pod. The fault-injection ConfigMap flagd-config holds 'adFailure' defaultVariant 'on' ('Fail ad service', state ENABLED) targeting the restarted/failing ad service, which per the investigation rules makes that ConfigMap the leading root-cause candidate; however the declared fault itself (ad service returning failures) was never observed — ad served normally from ~23:36:20Z with the flag still on — so the attribution is hypothesis-level and the conclusion is partial. A remaining candidate is that the ad container's 50m CPU limit turned the cold start into an ~8-minute outage through near-total CPU throttling.

claims.text: At 23:40:00Z, frontend-proxy's 5-minute increase of traces_span_metrics_calls_total shows error spans on both of its operations: span_name 'ingress' STATUS_CODE_ERROR 87.78 (vs 3626.67 UNSET) and span_name 'router frontend egress' STATUS_CODE_ERROR 72.22 (vs 3642.22 UNSET).

frontend-proxy's per-5m error-span increase was between 0 and 4.44 from 23:07:45Z through 23:27:45Z, then 121.11 at 23:29:45Z, 381.11 at 23:31:45Z, 614.44 at 23:33:45Z, 458.95 at 23:35:45Z, 404.44 at 23:37:45Z, 160.00 at 23:39:45Z, and back to 4.44 at 23:41:45Z (UNSET remained ~5.6k-7.6k per 5m).

The per-minute frontend-proxy error-span increase is 2 at 23:29:00Z and 212 at 23:30:00Z, stays at 84-242 per minute through 23:37:00Z (84), and is 0 at 23:38:00Z; i.e. the deviation began between 23:29:00Z and 23:30:00Z and ended by 23:38:00Z.

In the 10-minute window ending 23:40:00Z the error spans were concentrated in frontend 'GET' (356.84), 'GET /api/data' (356.84), 'executing api route (pages) /api/data' (356.84) and 'grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds' (356.84), plus frontend-proxy 'ingress' (373.68) and 'router frontend egress' (353.68); 'grpc.oteldemo.CartService/GetCart', 'grpc.oteldemo.CartService/AddItem', 'grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder', 'POST /api/cart', 'POST /api/checkout', payment 'GET', 'dns.lookup', 'tcp.connect', accounting 'orders receive', fraud-detection flagd spans and ad flagd spans all show 0 error spans in that window.

Frontend's client span 'grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds' in trace 139bb599d19f116ec39156d0b8506c04 (23:35:19Z) carries rpc.grpc.status_code=14 and the exact error '14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established. Last error: connect ECONNREFUSED 100.70.197.56:8080'; the same trace shows frontend 'GET /api/data' and 'executing api route (pages) /api/data' with http.status_code=500 and frontend-proxy 'ingress' and 'router frontend egress' with http.status_code=500.

A second sampled frontend error trace at 23:31:27Z shows the identical gRPC status 14 message 'No connection established. Last error: connect ECONNREFUSED 100.70.197.56:8080' on 'grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds' with frontend 'GET /api/data' 500 and frontend-proxy 'ingress'/'router frontend egress' 500.

Service ad has clusterIP 100.70.197.56 with port 8080 -> targetPort 8080 and selector opentelemetry.io/name=ad; the ad pod ad-785b4464f5-9bshh has podIP 100.96.3.224 and label opentelemetry.io/name=ad, so the refused address is ad's Service ClusterIP rather than the pod IP.

The ad service's server-side span 'oteldemo.AdService/GetAds' (service_name=ad, STATUS_CODE_UNSET) increased 161.33 per 2m at 23:29:00Z, then 1.33 at 23:31:00Z, 0 at 23:33:00Z, 0 at 23:35:00Z, 0 at 23:37:00Z and 140 at 23:39:00Z; ad served no GetAds requests between roughly 23:29:30Z and 23:38:00Z.

Frontend's client span 'grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds' shows 0 error spans through 23:29:00Z, then 140 (23:31:00Z), 82 (23:33:00Z), 152 (23:35:00Z), 86.67 (23:37:00Z) and 0 at 23:39:00Z, while its UNSET count fell from ~116-153 per 2m to 12, 0, 0 and 32 in the same interval.

Deployment ad was rolled out with an unchanged pod template: revision 2, container image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-ad and the same env set, the only pod-template difference recorded is the annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-17T23:28:05Z.

otel-demo events show Deployment ad 'Scaled up replica set ad-785b4464f5 from 0 to 1' at 23:28:05Z, pod ad-785b4464f5-9bshh Scheduled at 23:28:05Z, container Created at 23:28:06Z and Started at 23:28:07Z, ReplicaSet ad-554b849958 'Deleted pod: ad-554b849958-w5fhc' and Deployment ad 'Scaled down replica set ad-554b849958 from 1 to 0' at 23:28:07Z.

Pod ad-785b4464f5-9bshh is Running and Ready with 0 restarts and its ad container started at 2026-11-17T23:28:07Z; the frontend and frontend-proxy pods are also Running/Ready with 0 restarts (started 22:56:04Z and 22:56:04Z).
The ad container defines only containerPort 8080 and has no readinessProbe, livenessProbe or startupProbe; its resources are limits cpu 50m / memory 450Mi and requests cpu 10m / memory 225Mi.

The new ad container wrote no log output between 23:28 and ~23:36: its current instance holds 340 log lines, the first lines inside the 23:30:00-23:36:40Z window are at 23:36:33.744Z ('no baggage found in context'), and a query over 23:28:00-23:37:55Z returned only lines from 23:37:17Z onward among the newest 60.

The ad container's CFS throttling ratio (throttled periods / total periods, 2m rate) was 0.960 at 23:30:00Z, 1.0 at 23:32:00Z and 23:34:00Z, 1.0 at 23:36:00Z, then 0.420 at 23:38:00Z, 0.284 at 23:40:00Z and 0.263 at 23:42:00Z.

After ~23:36 the ad service served normally: 191.47 GetAds server spans per 10m ending 23:40:00Z, all STATUS_CODE_UNSET with no error status, and the ad container logs at 23:37:55Z-23:38:55Z show ordinary 'Targeted ad request received for [...]' / 'Non-targeted ad request received, preparing random response.' lines.
ConfigMap flagd-config in namespace otel-demo holds demo.flagd.json whose flag 'adFailure' has defaultVariant 'on', description 'Fail ad service' and state 'ENABLED'.

In the same demo.flagd.json every other fault-injection flag read is defaultVariant 'off': adHighCpu, adManualGc, cartFailure, emailMemoryLeak, imageSlowLoad, kafkaQueueProblems, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure.
The ad Deployment's env includes FLAGD_HOST=flagd and FLAGD_PORT=8013, so the ad service evaluates its feature flags from the flagd instance that serves flagd-config.

Alternative causes on the network/quota/service layer were checked and not found: the NetworkPolicy list for otel-demo returned no objects, the ResourceQuota list for otel-demo returned no objects, and Endpoints 'ad' currently resolves to pod ad-785b4464f5-9bshh at 100.96.3.224:8080, matching the Service selector.

The declared fault of the switched-on adFailure flag (the ad service failing requests) was not observed: ad's own GetAds spans carry no error status and ad served normal requests from ~23:36:20Z onward while the flag is still 'on', and the user-visible failures were connection refusals, not server-returned gRPC errors.

Leading root-cause candidate (hypothesis): the fault-injection setting held in ConfigMap flagd-config in otel-demo — 'adFailure' defaultVariant 'on', 'Fail ad service', state ENABLED, consumed by the ad service via FLAGD_HOST/FLAGD_PORT — is the fault origin; the ad Deployment restart at 23:28:05Z with an unchanged pod template and the ad service's unavailability from ~23:29:30Z to ~23:38:00Z are its mechanism, and the frontend GetAds UNAVAILABLE errors, frontend /api/data 500s and frontend-proxy error spans are its consequences.

Second remaining candidate (hypothesis): the ad container's 50m CPU limit (request 10m) starved the restarted container so its cold start never reached the listening state for ~8 minutes — supported by the 0.96-1.0 CFS throttling ratio during 23:30-23:36Z versus 0.26-0.42 after ~23:38Z and by the absence of any ad log line until ~23:36:20Z; the Deployment's pod template was unchanged, so the limit itself was not newly introduced.

Rejected: the fraud-detection container restart (previous instance terminated OOMKilled, exit code 137, finishedAt 2026-11-17T23:02:43Z, restartCount 1) as the cause of this alert — the failing operation was frontend->ad GetAds, the error burst began ~23:29Z (26 minutes after that OOM kill), and cart/checkout/payment/accounting related spans show 0 error spans in the 10m ending 23:40Z.

Rejected: a NetworkPolicy, ResourceQuota or Service/Endpoints misconfiguration between frontend and ad as the cause — otel-demo has no NetworkPolicy and no ResourceQuota objects, the ad Service selector opentelemetry.io/name=ad matches the ad pod's label, and the ad Endpoints contain that pod on port 8080.

Verify in flagd/flagd-ui whether the adFailure flag is intended to be 'on' for this environment and switch it off (as the other demo fault flags are) if the fault injection is finished; then re-check frontend 'grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds' error spans and frontend-proxy error spans.

Decouple ad availability from pod cold start: add a readinessProbe/startupProbe to the ad container so a not-yet-listening pod is removed from the ad Service endpoints, and raise the ad container's 50m CPU limit (or add a second replica / HPA) so a restarted single replica cannot be pinned at ~100% CFS throttling for minutes.

Identify who or what applied the kubectl rollout-restart annotation (kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-17T23:28:05Z) to Deployment ad and when adFailure was set to 'on', using an audit/change-history source that is not integrated in this Run.

gaps: Change history is not integrated in this Run: I cannot tell when flagd-config's adFailure defaultVariant was changed to 'on', nor who/what applied kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-17T23:28:05Z to Deployment ad.

The declared fault of the adFailure flag (ad service returning failures) was never observed during the window; the observed failure mode is connection refusal (gRPC 14) to the ad Service ClusterIP while the new ad pod was running but not serving.

No previous container instance exists for ad-785b4464f5-9bshh (HTTP 400 'previous terminated container not found') and the replaced pod ad-554b849958-w5fhc no longer exists, so the old pod's startup time and CPU-throttling baseline cannot be compared to the new pod's 8-minute start.

Queries for kube_pod_status_ready / kube_deployment_status_replicas_ready returned no series in this target, so pod readiness during 23:28-23:36Z is unknown beyond the fact that the ad container has no readiness probe (ready = container running).

A log query on the ad container for 'error|fail|exception|refused|unavailable' returned no lines (no_data view), which shows only that this query matched nothing; the absence of ad-side error logging is unproven, as is any ad-side explanation of the long startup.

Frontend container log lines matching 'error|fail|refused|unavailable' were not returned (no_data view), so the frontend's own log evidence for the 500s is unavailable; the error details come from its spans.

Kubernetes events are only those with timestamps inside 23:11:14Z-23:38:18Z and show possible timestamp skew (a 'Created container: fraud-detection' event at 23:34:55Z while that pod's current container started 23:02:43Z), so event timing is treated as approximate.

The Alertmanager alert start (23:26:45Z) precedes the observed error-rate deviation (between 23:29:00Z and 23:30:00Z); the metric the alert rule evaluates was not inspected, so the reason for that offset is unknown.

Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind.
